## Conference overview

*Preview by Adam Burke, p. 79. Reproduced in full.*


> From a College Football Playoff standpoint, the ACC had grown accustomed to leaving the party early until Miami showed up in a big way this past season.

> Clemson was a major player in the late 2010s, including two National Championships, but their one appearance in the last five seasons was a one-and-done as the No. 12 team in 2024.

> Florida State had a cameo appearance back in 2014 and relative newcomer SMU, who joined the conference in 2024, had a very short-lived appearance that same season.

> The Hurricanes were unable to finish the job and lost to Indiana, but Mario Cristobal was able to flip the proverbial bird to the doubters and haters with wins over Texas A&M, Ohio State, and Ole Miss before the 27-21 loss to the Hoosiers.

> The question now is whether or not Miami can piggyback off of that success.

> Because if they can’t, it looks like another season in which the ACC will be represented in the CFP simply by virtue of being a major conference with an automatic bid and having a seat at the table tall enough to get a team in the field.

> Incredibly, Miami didn’t even play in the ACC Championship Game last season, as that was between Duke and Virginia.

> The Blue Devils upset the Cavaliers, which kept Virginia out of the CFP.

> In the end, it worked out and the conference’s best team made the biggest statement in December and January.

> Despite some extremely heavy personnel losses, especially on defense, the Hurricanes (-136) still seem to have the inside track in the conference as a very clear odds-on favorite to celebrate in Charlotte on December 5.

> With SMU (7-1) and Louisville (8-1) as the only other teams lined in single digits to win the ACC at time of publish, it sure looks like the door is open for somebody to step up and challenge Miami.

> After all, five teams went 6-2 in conference play and five more went 4-4 last season.

> I’ll be nice and call it parity.

> Really, this just isn’t a very good conference top to bottom.

## Quarterback themes


**From the conference preview (p. 79):**

> *Not addressed in guide.*


**From the team pages in this conference** — 15 of 17 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Boston College Eagles** (p. 80) — Bill O’Brien has spent a big chunk of his coaching career working with quarterbacks and that has to be his primary focus for this season.

- **California Golden Bears** (p. 82) — For Lupoi, who has coached under some pretty esteemed mentors, this isn’t a total teardown and rebuild because of the presence of QB JaronKeawe Sagapolutele, but he will have a mostly blank slate to work with on defense.

- **Clemson Tigers** (p. 84) — Vizzina was a top-10 QB in his 2023 class per 247 and this is an excellent WR room.

- **Duke Blue Devils** (p. 86) — Having success at a program like Duke is more and more impressive with each passing season.

- **Florida State Seminoles** (p. 88) — Even if Daniels is an average QB, they can find their way into 7-5 or so, but I do think that the floor is lower than the ceiling is high.

- **Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets** (p. 90) — Key and the coaches had success with Texas A&M transfer Haynes King and they’ve turned to the portal again for Alberto Mendoza, the younger brother of Fernando Mendoza, the reigning National Championship QB and No. 1 overall pick.

- **Louisville Cardinals** (p. 92) — Brohm always finds ways to make the passing game work and this might be his first 200-yards-per-game rushing attack.

- **Miami Hurricanes** (p. 95) — He ultimately threw for over 3,800 yards and completed over 70% of his passes, but you have to wonder if Shannon Dawson’s offense has another gear with an objectively more talented QB.

## Returning-production themes


**From the conference preview (p. 79):**

> Florida State had a cameo appearance back in 2014 and relative newcomer SMU, who joined the conference in 2024, had a very short-lived appearance that same season.
>
> — *conference preview, p. 79*


**From the team pages in this conference** — 17 of 17 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Boston College Eagles** (p. 80) — He has virtually no D-I experience at the QB position heading into this season and very little in the way of returning production, but a team that went 2-10 needs an overhaul anyway and that’s precisely what has happened in Chestnut Hill, as the program looks to bounce back from its worst season since 2012.

- **California Golden Bears** (p. 83) — But, it was the offense that never really seemed to be able to get it going, despite a good amount of returning starters and returning production.

- **Clemson Tigers** (p. 84) — With scapegoat Garrett Riley gone and old friend Chad Morris back in the mix as OC, is a bounce back season imminent?

- **Duke Blue Devils** (p. 86) — The Blue Devils return their 1,100-yard rusher, but lose their QB, top three passcatchers, and Diaz has to mostly retool the defense with a handful of returnees, but only a couple of impact starters.

- **Florida State Seminoles** (p. 89) — Even with more production on both sides of the ball, the Seminoles were still -5 in TO margin and only mustered 14 takeaways in 12 games.

- **Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets** (p. 90) — With three straight losses to end the season, Georgia Tech’s last 10-win season moved another year back in the rearview mirror, but Brent Key got very close in his fourth full season at the helm.

- **Louisville Cardinals** (p. 92) — Since coming back in 2023, the Cardinals have won 10, 9, and 9 games, but have only made the ACC Title Game one time and have played in the Holiday, Sun, and Boca Raton Bowls.

- **Miami Hurricanes** (p. 95) — He’s been extremely well-coached throughout his career and enters a great situation here with Mark Fletcher & Co. all back at RB and 1,200yard WR Malachi Toney back to lead a rebuilt group that includes Mensah’s Duke teammate Cooper Barkate, who had 1,100 yards himself.

## Transfer-portal themes


**From the conference preview (p. 79):**

> *Not addressed in guide.*


**From the team pages in this conference** — 16 of 17 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Boston College Eagles** (p. 81) — The early leader in the clubhouse looks to be Saginaw Valley State transfer Mason McKenzie, who had zero FBS offers coming out of high school.

- **California Golden Bears** (p. 83) — He was originally committed to Oregon, but transferred to Cal to get a better opportunity prior to his freshman season.

- **Clemson Tigers** (p. 84) — Going 7-6 while under some scrutiny for being slow to react to the current landscape of college football and the transfer portal doesn’t sit well with a lot of deep-pocketed folks.

- **Duke Blue Devils** (p. 86) — For the third straight season, head coach Manny Diaz had to hit the transfer portal to find a QB, eventually going with San Jose State’s Walker Eget to replace Darian Mensah, who had a strong 34/6 TD/INT ratio last season.

- **Florida State Seminoles** (p. 89) — The majority of those passes and handoffs came from Tommy Castellanos, the Boston College transfer who led the team in rushing with just 557 yards and had a 15/9 TD/INT ratio.

- **Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets** (p. 90) — Key and the coaches had success with Texas A&M transfer Haynes King and they’ve turned to the portal again for Alberto Mendoza, the younger brother of Fernando Mendoza, the reigning National Championship QB and No. 1 overall pick.

- **Louisville Cardinals** (p. 93) — Miller Moss turned out not to be the answer, as the USC transfer took over for Tyler Shough and put up some pretty pedestrian numbers last season, falling short of 3,000 yards with just 16 TD passes.

- **NC State Wolfpack** (p. 97) — Backup QB Will Wilson is still around, as he was a short-yardage ball carrier with 10 touchdowns, but he only threw five passes, which means Coastal Carolina transfer Tad Hudson is the backup.

## Schedule themes


**From the conference preview (p. 79):**

> *Not addressed in guide.*


**From the team pages in this conference** — 17 of 17 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Boston College Eagles** (p. 80) — The Eagles don’t play in the best conference, but the only clear favorite role will be at home against Maine in Week 3.

- **California Golden Bears** (p. 82) — Being in the ACC presents a lot of logistical challenges and some rough travel, so depth is a priority with this program and it could take some time to build that up.

- **Clemson Tigers** (p. 84) — We’ll find out very quickly how Clemson looks for this season with the opener against LSU, but I have to think Swinney is beyond relieved to have Morris back, his OC from 2011-14.

- **Duke Blue Devils** (p. 86) — The schedule is a little tougher with Miami on the conference slate and the talent level of the program definitely seems to have dropped.

- **Florida State Seminoles** (p. 88) — With roadies at Alabama, Miami, and Louisville plus home games against SMU, Clemson, and Florida, it’s a tough-looking slate that leaves minimal margin for error.

- **Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets** (p. 90) — The schedule isn’t overly kind to the Yellow Jackets, especially late in the season.

- **Louisville Cardinals** (p. 92) — The conference schedule does not have Miami or Clemson and the games against SMU and Pitt are at home.

- **Miami Hurricanes** (p. 94) — With some raised expectations as the odds-on conference favorite, we’ll see if he can avoid those bumps in the road.

## Historical and situational notes


**From the conference preview (p. 79):**

> From a College Football Playoff standpoint, the ACC had grown accustomed to leaving the party early until Miami showed up in a big way this past season.
>
> — *conference preview, p. 79*

> Clemson was a major player in the late 2010s, including two National Championships, but their one appearance in the last five seasons was a one-and-done as the No. 12 team in 2024.
>
> — *conference preview, p. 79*

> Florida State had a cameo appearance back in 2014 and relative newcomer SMU, who joined the conference in 2024, had a very short-lived appearance that same season.
>
> — *conference preview, p. 79*

> Incredibly, Miami didn’t even play in the ACC Championship Game last season, as that was between Duke and Virginia.
>
> — *conference preview, p. 79*

> After all, five teams went 6-2 in conference play and five more went 4-4 last season.
>
> — *conference preview, p. 79*


**From the team pages in this conference** — 17 of 17 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Boston College Eagles** (p. 80) — Dylan Lonergan and Grayson James split time last season, collectively posting a 19/10 TD/ INT ratio, but this was a very poor football team.

- **California Golden Bears** (p. 82) — The Walnut Creek native played at Cal from 2000-05 and also got his coaching career underway there in 2008.

- **Clemson Tigers** (p. 84) — The defense was extremely good last season and it shouldn’t take much for the offense to improve with the pipeline of talent Dabo has established.

- **Duke Blue Devils** (p. 86) — For the third straight season, head coach Manny Diaz had to hit the transfer portal to find a QB, eventually going with San Jose State’s Walker Eget to replace Darian Mensah, who had a strong 34/6 TD/INT ratio last season.

- **Florida State Seminoles** (p. 89) — The Seminoles were 0-5 on the road last season and 2-6 overall in conference play.

- **Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets** (p. 90) — We have no idea what to expect from him since Curt Cignetti rarely took his foot off the gas at Indiana and he didn’t play very much.

- **Louisville Cardinals** (p. 92) — Since coming back in 2023, the Cardinals have won 10, 9, and 9 games, but have only made the ACC Title Game one time and have played in the Holiday, Sun, and Boca Raton Bowls.

- **Miami Hurricanes** (p. 94) — The other ACC teams were Florida State in 2014 and SMU in 2024 prior to the Hurricanes’ run last season.
